newsitem.title: UGANDA: Ugandan newspaper editor detained, staff say.
newsitem.headline: Ugandan newspaper editor detained, staff say.

text.p: The editor of a weekly Ugandan newspaper that quoted Zairean sources as saying Rwandan and Ugandan troops and rebels were killing thousands of refugees in eastern Zaire was arrested and charged on Wednesday, staff said.
Peter Mungherera, the deputy editor of the Uganda Express weekly, said editor Peter Busiku was asked to call at Criminal Investigation Department headquarters and was then arrested.
He said Busiky was later charged in a Kampala court with publishing false and alarming reports, remanded in custody and was scheduled to appear in the same court again on Thursday.
Mungherera said police objected to a story quoting Zairean sources published a week ago saying Ugandan and Rwandan troops and Tutsi rebels were killing thousands of refugees in eastern Zaire.

He said the paper also quoted Zairean sources saying Ugandan President Yoweri Museveni, Rwandan military strongman Paul Kagame and Burundi military ruler Pierre Buyoya met to plot a genocidal attack on Hutu Rwandan refugees in camps in Tanzania.
Uganda, Rwanda and Burundi deny Zairean accusations that their armies are fighting alongside Tutsi rebels in east Zaire.
